title: Newton's Inequality, First Rung (n = 3): S₂² ≥ S₁S₃

problemStatement.formal: For a b c : ℝ, with e₁ = a+b+c, e₂ = ab+bc+ca, e₃ = abc, and S₁ = e₁/3, S₂ = e₂/3, S₃ = e₃: S₂² ≥ S₁·S₃, equivalently e₂² ≥ 3·e₁·e₃.
problemStatement.plain: Prove the next Maclaurin/Newton rung after the base step S₁² ≥ S₂, namely S₂² ≥ S₁S₃ (log-concavity of the elementary symmetric means), for n = 3.
whyMatters: First rung of the Maclaurin/Newton chain that carries genuine content beyond Cauchy-Schwarz.
Newton's inequalities hold for all reals (not just nonnegative), unlike Maclaurin's chain.

open: Full Newton chain S_k² ≥ S_{k-1}S_{k+1} for all k

insights: At n=3 Newton's inequality is literally a three-term sum of squares, so no Rolle's theorem / discriminant machinery is needed — the whole proof stays inside real-closed-field arithmetic (ring + nlinarith).
This rung is strictly beyond Cauchy-Schwarz: the base rung S₁²≥S₂ reduces to the power-mean bound n·p₂≥e₁², but S₂²≥S₁S₃ has no such reduction; its content is the fresh SOS certificate.
No nonnegativity hypothesis is required — the SOS certificate is sign-agnostic, so S₂²≥S₁S₃ holds for all real a,b,c (nonnegativity only matters at Maclaurin rungs that extract real roots).
The equality locus is exactly ab=bc=ca (⇒ a=b=c for nonzero variables), read directly off the vanishing of the three squared pairwise-product differences.
The general-n cleared form is 2(n−2)e₂² ≥ 3(n−1)e₁e₃, reducing to e₂²≥3e₁e₃ at n=3; its general proof needs the Rolle/derivative real-rootedness argument.
nextSteps: General-n k=2 Newton inequality via Rolle's theorem on ∏(x−xᵢ) and its derivatives.
